caption:
A report on 24 September 2026 flags rising burnout among middle managers at Indian professional services firms — and it does not call it a wellness issue. It calls it an operational and financial risk.

Read that again. The strain in the middle of your org chart is now a margin problem.

Here is the position you are actually in: enough responsibility to be blamed, not enough authority to be heard. You carry the delivery. You absorb the escalation. You present the plan and watch it get adopted only after someone senior repeats it back.

That is not a character flaw. That is a positional flaw. You are operating without command authority in a role that demands it.

In 35 years of military command, Colonel Suhag saw the same pattern: capable officers undermined not by competence but by bearing. Authority is signalled before it is granted. Posture, tone, calculated silence — these are trainable.

Fix the position. The exhaustion follows.

topic.title: Middle-management burnout now a margin risk, not a mood
topic.angle: Lumina's buyer is the squeezed middle manager with enough responsibility to be blamed and not enough authority to be heard, and this reframes their struggle as positional rather than personal inadequacy.
topic.why_now: A piece published 24 September 2026 reports rising burnout among middle managers at Indian professional services firms and frames it as an operational and financial risk — the only India-specific, seniority-specific workplace item dated inside the last week.

rationale: A stark text-only visual on a dark field matches the plainspoken, command-authority tone and lets the positional reframe land without decoration.
